section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1967
title: ## All-India Survey During 1967, 1,26,762 deaths were reported in India which had resulted from accidents. Out of this total 36,313 deaths (28·7% of the total incidence) were due to acts of nature such as snake-bites, floods, land-slides, lightning, heat-strokes and others. 90,449 cases (71·3% of the total incidence) were due to other forms of accidents such as those on roads, those due to air crashes and others resulting from mishappenings in factories, railways etc. Table I presents the actual and percentage incidence of accidental deaths during 1967 due to various causes. It has been observed that the most prominent accidental killer was drowning (24·7% of total deaths due to all causes together). Accidents on roads and railways accounted for 4·9% and 5·6% of deaths respectively. Fire and animal bites/killing were responsible for 6·5% and 3·5% of deaths respectively. The pattern of percentage distribution of incidence due to various causes is more or less the same as during 1965 and 1966. TABLE—1
